title: Player-facing character creation intake form (session-zero backstory writing that shapes the campaign)
summary: Players log into Foundry and build their kid PC through a form that tone-sets the setting (welcoming, queer/LGBTQ+-aware Golarion, found-family theme) and frames enrollment in-fiction as mandatory Civil Defence Force clearance, including a DNA test that flags unexplained 'irregularities.' A free-text backstory prompt invites players to write as much or as little as they want about their character; that writing directly shapes how the GM and Claude build campaign content for them. v1 latency is session-boundary (write, sync, GM+Claude read and respond next session); live mid-session response via OpenRouter is named explicitly as a later, separate stretch goal.
description:
First installment of a user 'rant' (explicitly flagged as ongoing/multi-part) about what session zero should feel like, given right after the Foundry diagnostic test sync succeeded (15/15 checks) and the user chose 'the fun bit' — character-facing creative work — as the next focus over continuing module plumbing.

Pieces described so far:

1. **Login and form flow**: players log into the Foundry page and fill out a form to create their student character. Not yet specified whether this is a real ApplicationV2 form, a journal-based intake, or something else — ties naturally to the existing terminal-login-landing-page idea (that one is the login/boot-screen shell; this could be what a new player lands in after authenticating).

2. **Tone-setting inside the form itself**: hints at the setting being Golarion (consistent with, not new relative to, the already-accepted golarion-grounding-touches idea), and states directly that this is a welcoming, queer-friendly, LGBTQ+-aware universe. The school's kids often hide secrets about themselves. The throughline the user wants surfaced: Found Family — being chosen by friends who help you endure hard times and a sometimes grim-looking future. This sits alongside, not in place of, the self-determination/independence theme already recorded in campaign-arc.md's Core Theme section — worth folding in as a second thematic pillar once the rest of this rant is in, rather than editing that section on this one installment alone.

3. **In-fiction enrollment framing — a candidate discovery vector for the ancestry-reveal mechanic**: sign-up establishes that the character already underwent a mandatory DNA test as part of Civil Defence Force clearance. The test flagged 'irregularities' that were hard to explain, but the character was otherwise healthy and cleared for active duty. This is a clean, diegetic answer to part of the then-open ancestry-reveal-justification question (data/campaign/open-questions.json) — the discovery vector (a mandatory clearance DNA test) is now a concrete proposal, though the deeper explanation (why the DNA reads irregular, how it connects to Anabala/the Mitflits) was still open. Reflected in that question's resolution text as of this capture. (Moved on since: the blood test is taken in play, by Shucks at Intake Medicals in Episode One, and what it flags is mitflit DNA, which all six PCs carry and which a pilot needs to fly a Gen 2 Frame; LEDGER #20, #21 and #34.)

4. **Backstory writing as a campaign-shaping input, not flavor text**: players are invited to write about things that happened to their character — as little or as much as they want, explicitly framed as a chance to gush about their character concept. That writing is used to inform how the campaign gets built for that character. Explicit stated goal: 'make everyone happy, not just the GM' — a campaign that lets players actually influence content, not just react to GM-authored content. This is session zero's version of the same pattern already captured in in-universe-correspondence-negotiation-system (player writes in-fiction content -> it syncs to files -> GM and Claude read it and collaboratively build the response/content) — that idea covers ongoing mid-campaign negotiation (gear, mechs, requests); this one covers the one-time (or rare) session-zero backstory intake that seeds a character's campaign content in the first place. Likely siblings under the same eventual sync mechanism, not the same idea.

5. **Latency is an explicit, named design choice, not a limitation being apologized for**: v1 always has a session-boundary gap — write during/before a session, sync, GM and Claude read it between sessions, respond in the next one. The user explicitly named a possible future upgrade: OpenRouter-mediated live response mid-session, and explicitly scoped that as 'end game stuff' — a distinct, later technical layer, not something v1 needs to support. Worth keeping this scope line sharp: the async version should be fully buildable and valuable on its own, not designed as a stepping-stone that only works once live response exists.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — first installment of a stated multi-part rant about session-zero character creation, given as the user's chosen next focus after the Foundry diagnostic test sync passed 15/15.
openSubQuestions: Exact form technology — real Foundry ApplicationV2 UI, a structured journal, or something else.

How backstory prose actually travels from Foundry back to the repo for Claude to read — presumably the harvest mechanism (design/foundry-module-design.md §4), but not confirmed as the same pipeline as the correspondence system.
Whether backstory intake is a one-time session-zero event or stays open/editable later in the campaign.
Still waiting on the rest of the user's rant (explicitly flagged as continuing) before treating this capture as complete.

How this reconciles with the standing project rule that the six kids/Frames are collaborative creative work not to be invented unilaterally — this form is presumably the mechanism THROUGH WHICH that collaboration happens for the real six, not a way around it.
resolution: ACCEPTED and substantially expanded 2026-09-09 — see design/induction.md §3. The form is no longer a session-zero questionnaire sitting outside the fiction: it is the Directorate's own induction terminal, and filling it in is the character-creation SCENE. Two features were added on top of bible §20's eight intake questions. (1) A per-player HELP TOGGLE: every question has an in-character layer and an out-of-character layer explaining what it is actually asking and how to answer it usefully, so nobody has to guess what they are feeding the campaign and nobody has immersion broken who did not ask for it. Same one-line-plus-peekable-detail idiom as the scene runner. (2) An ALIEN LOCKDOWN easter egg: every PC presents as human/elf/halfling at the start and any non-terrestrial ancestry trips the screen, whereupon the terminal locks down and asks — bureaucratically, patiently — how they have gone undetected for seventeen years. Fires on that player's screen only, so the reveal stays theirs to make; the table just sees somebody go quiet. Not yet built.
